meta.title: Temporal Knowledge Graph Completion: A Survey
meta.paper_type_explanation: The paper comprehensively summarizes recent advances in Temporal Knowledge Graph Completion (TKGC) research, categorizing methods, datasets, and evaluation protocols without proposing a new model or system.

A_data_and_task.domain_data_type_explanation: Focuses on temporal knowledge graphs from event repositories and knowledge bases, such as geopolitical events and wiki data.
A_data_and_task.task_type_explanation: Primary task is predicting missing links in temporal knowledge graphs using temporal validity of facts to capture dynamics.

dataset_size.relations: Varies: ICEWS14 (230), ICEWS05-15 (251), ICEWS18 (256), GDELT (20), YAGO15k (32), WIKIDATA (96)

A_data_and_task.dataset_characteristics_explanation: Datasets include point timestamps (ICEWS, GDELT) and range timestamps (YAGO15k, WIKIDATA); GDELT has largest facts but abstract entities challenge performance.
A_data_and_task.benchmark_metrics_explanation: Metrics evaluate link prediction accuracy via ranking true facts among candidates; applied to entity, relation, and time prediction.

B_graph_kg_structure.graph_kg_representation_type_explanation: Knowledge graphs represented as directed multi-relational graphs with temporal validity in facts (quadruples: head, relation, tail, timestamp).
B_graph_kg_structure.graph_evolution_type_explanation: Survey assumes invariant graphs for TKGC evaluation; future work notes need for evolutionary graphs with updates.
B_graph_kg_structure.node_types_explanation: Nodes are entities; no mention of events, documents, or other specialized nodes.
B_graph_kg_structure.edge_types_explanation: Edges are relations connecting entities; augmented inverse relations for bidirectional prediction.
B_graph_kg_structure.graph_schema_explanation: No explicit schema discussion; datasets imply fixed relations per benchmark.
B_graph_kg_structure.graph_scale_explanation: Benchmark datasets range from ~7K to 23K entities, aligning with medium scale.

C_temporal_modeling_and_queries.temporal_structure_type_explanation: Facts include timestamps (points or ranges split into points); captures evolution via representations.
C_temporal_modeling_and_queries.temporal_granularity_explanation: Timestamps as points (e.g., 2010) or ranges (e.g., 2010-2013) discretized to points.
C_temporal_modeling_and_queries.temporal_representation_explanation: Timestamps treated as discrete points; ranges split for convenience.
C_temporal_modeling_and_queries.temporal_query_handling_explanation: No explicit query handling; focus on link prediction with given timestamps.
C_temporal_modeling_and_queries.multi_hop_temporal_reasoning_explanation: Some methods (e.g., xERTE, T-GAP) use multi-hop paths with temporal attention/displacement.

D_dynamic_update_mechanisms.verification_pipeline_explanation: Not applicable to survey; future work mentions continual learning for updates.
D_dynamic_update_mechanisms.update_latency_throughput_explanation: Notes training on benchmarks takes hours-days; calls for distributed models.

E_retrieval_and_reasoning.retrieval_strategy_explanation: Categorizes methods including reasoning with historical context (attention/heuristic) and snapshots (GNNs).
E_retrieval_and_reasoning.reasoning_generation_protocol_explanatio: Methods like xERTE (subgraph expansion), T-GAP (attention flow), TLmod (rules).
E_retrieval_and_reasoning.multi_hop_reasoning_support_explanation: Supports via path reasoning in historical context methods.

F_llm_role_and_learning.llm_role_in_system_explanation: Pre-LLM era survey; no LLM discussion.
F_llm_role_and_learning.continual_learning_support_explanation: Future direction: continual learning for evolving graphs to avoid retraining.

G_evaluation_and_practical.evaluation_focus_explanation: Accuracy on link prediction; challenges with unseen timestamps (future/missing).
G_evaluation_and_practical.evaluation_metrics_explanation: Hits@k (percentage ranks ≤k), MR (avg rank), MRR (inverse avg rank).
G_evaluation_and_practical.baseline_comparisons_explanation: No direct comparisons due to implementation differences; summarizes TKGC vs KGC improvements.
G_evaluation_and_practical.explainability_explanation: Rule-based (TLogic, TLmod) and path methods (xERTE, T-GAP) provide interpretable reasoning.
G_evaluation_and_practical.scalability_analysis_explanation: Benchmarks time-consuming; real-world graphs need distributed/compositional approaches.

H_novel_technical_contributions.algorithmic_innovations_explanation: Proposes taxonomy based on timestamp integration: tensor decomposition, time-based transformation, dynamic embedding, snapshots, historical reasoning, logical rules.
H_novel_technical_contributions.neural_architecture_explanation: Summarizes GNNs for snapshots, RNNs for dynamics.

I_reproducibility_implementation.code_availability_explanation: No code provided; notes implementation differences prevent performance comparisons.
I_reproducibility_implementation.hyperparameters_explanation: Mentions losses (margin ranking, cross-entropy, binary cross-entropy).

J_limitations_future_work.acknowledged_limitations_explanation: Low accuracy on GDELT due to abstract entities; lacks time-aware negatives, external knowledge.
J_limitations_future_work.future_research_directions_explanation: Incorporate external knowledge, time-aware negatives, distributed training, continual learning for updates.

main_findings: TKGC outperforms static KGC; challenges in scalability and generalization

notable_contributions_explanation: First comprehensive TKGC survey with taxonomy, dataset summary, and future directions.

related_papers_mentioned: Many TKGC methods (e.g., TTransE, HyTE, Know-Evolve); KGC baselines (TransE)
extraction_metadata.extraction_notes: Paper is a survey, so many fields N/A; focuses on embedding/representation methods pre-LLM/GraphRAG era. No DOI/link extracted from text.
